features.definition: The most the policy pays for surgery costs, per person per year.
The cap on hospital treatment that isn't surgery (e.g. medical admissions).
What you can choose to pay yourself per claim/year in exchange for lower premiums.
What cancer treatment is covered and up to how much.
Cover for effective drugs NZ's public system doesn't fund — one of the biggest real differences between NZ policies.
Cover for surveillance/check-ups after cancer treatment.
Cover for private specialist visits — capped amount, and whether GP referral is required.
MRI, CT, and other tests — what's covered, any caps, any time-link to surgery.
Whether tests/consultations must relate to treatment within a set window to be claimable.
How each insurer treats conditions you had before joining — excluded, covered after a period, or reviewable.
How long after joining before specific benefits can be claimed.
Whether and when conditions present from birth are covered.
Optional module for everyday costs: GP visits, prescriptions, dental, optical.
Any cover for pregnancy-related care.
Any cover for psychiatric/psychological care.
Remote GP/specialist consultations covered or provided.
Caps and lists for implants and devices used in surgery.
Whether you must use the insurer's affiliated providers for full cover.
Whether treatment must be approved before you book it.
How claims are made and typical settlement approach.
Extra benefits that accrue the longer you hold the policy.
How premiums change with age/claims (community-rated vs age-rated).
Whether improvements to the policy automatically apply to existing members.
The main things this policy will never pay for.
Any age at which cover ends or changes.

sc.value: Unlimited for eligible surgical procedures performed by a specialist or Affiliated Provider (individual prostheses limits apply). Excess applies to this benefit.

No single standalone non-surgical hospitalisation cap. Non-surgical cover is provided through named benefits instead (e.g. imaging $60,000/yr, cardiac tests $5,000/yr, diagnostic tests $3,000/yr, psychiatric admission $3,500/yr). NEEDS CARE IN PHRASING — verify framing.
Excess options offered; chosen amount shown on membership certificate. Excess applies per person, once per claims year, and only to the surgical procedures, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy benefits.

Chemotherapy (base): 100% of actual charges up to $60,000 each claims year for Pharmac-approved treatment via Affiliated Provider; excess applies. Radiotherapy: 100% of actual charges for a limited range of treatments (no annual dollar cap stated); excess applies.

Base plan: non-Pharmac (Medsafe-indicated) chemotherapy drugs up to $10,000 each claims year. Optional Cancer Cover Plus upgrades lift this: Chemotherapy 100 = $100,000/yr; Chemotherapy 300 = $300,000/yr (upgrades exclude cancers with defined family history).

On Wellbeing Two, specialist consultations, imaging, and tests are NOT time-limited to treatment (the 6-month rule applies to Wellbeing One only). Oncologist consultations always exempt from time rules.
Specialist consultations up to $5,000 each claims year (100% of actual charges; includes second opinions via contracted Affiliated Providers). Psychiatrist consultations separately capped at $750/yr.

Diagnostic imaging up to $60,000 each claims year (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray; PET/CT for specific cancers and cardiac conditions; no excess). Cardiac tests $5,000/yr; diagnostic tests $3,000/yr; laboratory tests $70/yr (Wellbeing Two benefit).
None on Wellbeing Two. (Wellbeing One requires consults/imaging/tests within 6 months of related surgery, chemo, or radiotherapy.)

Pre-existing conditions are not covered unless explicitly accepted and stated on the membership certificate (individually underwritten at application). Exclusion does not apply to the optional day-to-day modules.

No general stand-down stated, but specific benefits carry qualifying periods: obstetrics allowance after 1 year continuous cover (Wellbeing Two); complete skin-lesion removal after 3 years continuous cover.
Excluded, except: umbilical hernia, inguinal hernia, undescended testes, hydrocele, tongue tie, phimosis, and squint.
Two optional modules: 'Keeping Well Module' and 'Day-to-day Module' (prescriptions, physiotherapy and similar day-to-day costs).
Wellbeing Two only: obstetrics allowance $750 each claims year after 1 year continuous cover (specialist obstetric care, 2D/Doppler ultrasounds, approved-facility accommodation); no excess.
Psychiatrist consultations $750 each claims year; psychiatric admission & care $3,500 each claims year (sub-limits apply).
Not specified in the policy wording. Southern Cross promotes member telehealth services (e.g. Care Hub) outside the policy document — VERIFY from SC website before publishing anything.
sc.source: PD_Wellbeing_plan.pdf (eff. 1 Apr 2026) · not found in wording

sc.value: Covered as part of eligible surgery per the separate 'List of prostheses and specialised equipment', which sets a maximum payment per item (southerncross.co.nz/lopse). Surgical benefit is unlimited but each prosthesis is individually capped.

Strong Affiliated Provider model: some services are Affiliated-Provider-only (separate list); using an AP means they arrange prior approval and claim directly. Non-AP use may expose you to 'reasonable charges' gaps.

Recommended at least 5 working days before treatment; required for some benefits (e.g. overseas treatment, $40k lifetime treatment benefit). Not needed when an Affiliated Provider performs a contracted service (they arrange it).
Online via MySouthernCross or the app; Affiliated Providers and Easy-Claim partners claim directly on your behalf.
No broad loyalty programme in the wording; time-based benefit unlocks instead (obstetrics after 1 yr on Two; full skin-lesion removal after 3 yrs).
Not stated in the policy document (premiums set outside the wording; SC re-prices with age at renewal). Source externally before publishing — EXTERNAL VERIFICATION NEEDED.

Southern Cross may change the policy document over time and changes apply to existing members (policyholder may cancel if they disagree). Membership certificate takes precedence over the policy document.

Headline exclusions: pre-existing conditions (unless accepted), a defined list of chronic conditions, congenital conditions (with the exceptions above), termination of pregnancy, most breast reconstruction/symmetry beyond named benefits, overseas treatment beyond the $30,000/yr benefit.
No ceasing age identified in the policy wording — verify (SC membership is generally lifetime-renewable).
sc.source: PD_Wellbeing_plan.pdf (eff. 1 Apr 2026) · not found in wording

nib.value: Surgical Benefit: up to $600,000 per insured person every policy year for private hospital surgery. Several related benefits (diagnostics, cancer treatment, travel) draw from this limit.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Surgical Benefit' section

nib.value: Non-Surgical Benefit: up to $300,000 per insured person every policy year for non-surgical private hospital admission.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Non-Surgical Benefit' section

nib.value: Excess applies per policy (amount on Acceptance/Renewal Certificate); some benefits explicitly excess-free (e.g. Loyalty Sterilisation). EXCESS OPTION AMOUNTS NOT IN WORDING — verify options from nib site/application.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · benefit terms + certificate

nib.value: Cancer Treatment Benefit: cancer treatment paid from the remaining Surgical ($600k) or Non-Surgical ($300k) limit — cancer surgery under Surgical. No separate lower cancer cap; private-hospital suites excluded.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Cancer Treatment Benefit' section

nib.value: Non-PHARMAC Cancer Treatment Benefit: chemotherapy/immunotherapy medicines not funded by PHARMAC, administered in private hospital — up to $20,000 per insured person every policy year. (Ultimate Health Max lifts this substantially — extract Max next.)
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Non-PHARMAC Cancer Treatment Benefit' section

nib.value: Cancer follow-up: investigations relating to your cancer up to $3,000 per person per policy year (requires a related paid claim).
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · cancer follow-up benefit

nib.value: Hospital Specialist Consultations: unlimited during admission period (requires related Surgical/Non-Surgical claim). Pre/post-surgery consultations up to $6,000/yr. Optional Specialist Option adds standalone specialist consults (unlimited number) without needing an admission.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Hospital Specialist Consultations' + Specialist Option

nib.value: Diagnostic Investigations: unlimited number of tests, paid from the remaining Surgical/Non-Surgical limit (requires related claim). Specialist Option adds standalone imaging (MRI, CT etc.) up to $60,000/yr and surveillance imaging $3,000/yr.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Diagnostic Investigations' + Specialist Option

nib.value: Base diagnostics/consultations are tied to a related Surgical or Non-Surgical claim rather than a time window. Specialist Option benefits need only a GP/specialist referral.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · benefit conditions

nib.value: Underwritten at application: pre-existing conditions typically become personal exclusions listed on your Acceptance Certificate (or premium loadings). NOTE: optional Options (GP, Dental etc.) cover pre-existing conditions EXCEPT congenital — a genuine nib point of difference.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · certificate terms + Options sections

nib.value: Base Cover: from join date (per certificate). Options carry waits: GP-type Option 90 days; Dental/Optical-type Option 6 months; Loyalty benefits are time-based (e.g. Sterilisation after 2 years).
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'When will I be covered?' sections

nib.value: Congenital conditions excluded (defined as recognised at birth or diagnosed within 4 months of birth). General exclusions list congenital/chromosomal disorders, Marfan's, gene therapy, genetic testing.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · exclusions + glossary

nib.value: Optional GP Option: GP consults up to $55 each ($80 home, $25 ACC top-up), prescriptions $15/item to $300/yr, physio-type treatments $40/visit to $400/yr, nurse visits $30 × 6. Dental/Optical/Therapeutic Option also available.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · GP Option + DOT Option

nib.value: No general obstetrics benefit. High-Risk Pregnancy Benefit covers obstetrician assessment/monitoring of recognised risk factors only; excludes normal pregnancy, pregnancies conceived before join date, public hospital treatment.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'High-Risk Pregnancy Benefit'

nib.value: No standalone mental health benefit identified in Base Cover — VERIFY before publishing (check Non-Surgical Benefit scope and any counselling benefits in full doc).
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · needs second pass

nib.value: Not identified in wording — nib promotes telehealth/virtual GP services outside the policy document. VERIFY from nib site.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · not found in wording

nib.value: Prostheses handling not extracted on first pass — VERIFY (nib typically covers per schedule within Surgical Benefit).
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · needs second pass

nib.value: 'Recognised providers' — you can use any recognised NZ provider; nib's First Choice Network is preferred (pre-approvals honoured regardless of later status changes). Claims priced against nib's 'Efficient Market Price' — non-First-Choice providers may leave a gap.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Using your cover'

nib.value: Pre-approval recommended via 'my nib' before treatment; locks in the Efficient Market Price at pre-approval date. Without it, price applies at treatment date.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Using your cover'

nib.value: Claims and pre-approvals through the 'my nib' portal/app.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · 'Using your cover'

nib.value: Distinct loyalty layer: Loyalty benefits unlock over time — Sterilisation (after 2 yrs), Check Up ($100 every 3 yrs), Orthodontic, Active Wellness, Health Check, cover-suspension benefit.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · Loyalty benefits

nib.value: Not stated in policy document (nib prices by age/plan at renewal). EXTERNAL VERIFICATION NEEDED.
nib.source: External — nib website/application

nib.value: Policy terms can change at renewal (Acceptance/Renewal Certificate governs). Whether wording improvements auto-apply to existing members not confirmed on first pass — VERIFY.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · needs second pass

nib.value: Key exclusions: personal exclusions per certificate (pre-existing), congenital/chromosomal disorders, genetic testing/therapy, normal pregnancy, public hospital treatment, private hospital suites; general exclusions list applies.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · exclusions section

nib.value: No ceasing age identified on first pass — VERIFY.
nib.source: nib Ultimate Health Base Policy Document (eff. 1 Feb 2024+) · needs second pass

aia.value: Surgery benefit: Unlimited (reasonable charges) in an approved facility, incl. surgeon/anaesthetist/hospital fees and prostheses. Includes related outpatient consults, imaging and tests within 12 months before/after surgery. Excess applies.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.10–11

aia.value: Medical Hospitalisation: $500,000 per life assured per policy year for non-surgical private hospital treatment (specialist-referred). Cancer hospitalisation sits under Cancer Care instead. Excess applies.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · p.14

aia.value: Excess options: $0, $250, $500, $750, $1,000, $2,000, $4,000 or $10,000 (Private Health Cover). Private Health Plus additional benefits: $0 or $250. Many benefits are explicitly excess-free.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · p.7 (§E)

aia.value: Cancer Care benefit: $500,000 per life assured per policy year for non-surgical cancer treatment (consults, imaging, chemo/immunotherapy, radiotherapy, brachytherapy); cancer surgery under the unlimited Surgery benefit. Also covers prophylactic mastectomy/oophorectomy (BRCA1/2), breast reconstruction and symmetry surgery, and post-cancer support (psychologist, wigs, home help).
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.11–13

aia.value: Non-Pharmac cancer medicines: covered WITHIN the $500,000/yr Cancer Care benefit — Pharmac and non-Pharmac Medsafe-indicated chemo/immunotherapy (incl. targeted therapy, oral, at home), subject to AIA criteria and prior approval. No separate low non-Pharmac cap in this product.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.11–12

aia.value: Post-cancer treatment care and support benefit (psychologist consults, personal items, lymphatic massage, home help); surgery-related follow-up consults/imaging within 12 months of surgery.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.10, 13

aia.value: Base: specialist consults covered when directly related to approved surgery (within 12 months) or cancer treatment. Private Health Plus adds standalone Specialist Consultations up to $10,000/yr (GP-referred). Excess applies.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.10, 21

aia.value: Major Diagnostic Imaging and Tests (base): $200,000 per life assured per policy year, specialist-referred, surgery not required (CT, MRI, PET/CT, colonoscopy, angiogram etc.). Private Health Plus adds broader Diagnostic Imaging & Tests at $100,000/yr on GP referral (incl. labs, X-ray, ultrasound, sleep studies).
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.15, 21–22

aia.value: Surgery-related outpatient support: 12 months before/after surgery (consults, imaging); physio/OT/prescriptions within 6 months after surgery.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.10–11

aia.value: Underwritten: pre-existing conditions excluded/personally excluded per schedule (standard AIA approach). Notable exception: the Congenital Conditions Surgery benefit is exempt from the pre-existing exclusion.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.14–15, 23–25

aia.value: Pregnancy/maternity allowance (Plus) requires 2 years continuous cover; several benefits require 3 years continuous cover (see wording pp.19–20 — VERIFY specifics); 15-day free-look period.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.1, 19–22

aia.value: Congenital Conditions Surgery benefit: $2,000 per life per LIFETIME for the same 7 conditions others merely exempt from exclusion (umbilical/inguinal hernia, undescended testes, hydrocele, tongue tie, phimosis, squint); no excess; prior approval required.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.14–15

aia.value: No GP/day-to-day module in this product. Private Health Plus tier adds GP-referred specialist consults, wider diagnostics, health screening allowance.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.21–22

aia.value: Pregnancy, Maternity and Infertility Allowance (Plus only): $1,500 per pregnancy per policy year (obstetric care incl. scans, infertility diagnosis/treatment, related accommodation) after 2 years continuous Plus cover; no excess. Caesarean-related benefit noted separately ($2,000, caesarean excluded from one benefit — VERIFY which).
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.19, 22

aia.value: No general psychiatric/mental health hospitalisation benefit identified; psychologist support covered post-cancer only. VERIFY against exclusions list.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.13, 23–25

aia.value: Not in policy wording. AIA runs the separate AIA Vitality wellness programme (premium discounts) outside this policy — reference as a programme, not a policy benefit.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · not found in wording

aia.value: Prostheses included within Surgery benefit inpatient costs (unlimited benefit; reasonable charges apply). No separate prostheses schedule cited in wording — VERIFY whether internal limits exist.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · p.10

aia.value: 'Approved facility' model — treatment must be in approved facilities; 'reasonable charges' standard applies across benefits. No affiliated-provider-style network restrictions equivalent to SC/nib identified.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · benefit terms + defined terms

aia.value: Prior approval required for many benefits (all cancer treatments, prophylactic surgery, congenital surgery, overseas-related benefits). Apply via aia.co.nz or 0800 500 108.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.2, 4–5, 11–15

aia.value: Claims via aia.co.nz / 0800 500 108 (§D 'How to make a claim').
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.4–6

aia.value: Time-based benefit unlocks at 2 and 3 years continuous cover (details pp.19–22 — VERIFY list); AIA Vitality (separate programme) offers premium discounts up to material levels.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.19–22 + AIA site

aia.value: Not stated in policy document. EXTERNAL VERIFICATION NEEDED (AIA prices by age; Vitality discounts affect net premium).
aia.source: External — AIA website/application

aia.value: Enhancement Pass Back Benefit (§B): future improvements to the policy are automatically passed back to existing policyholders — a distinctive AIA feature; changes via pass-back don't require the 30-day notice.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.3, §F

aia.value: Exclusions section pp.23–25: pre-existing conditions, plus standard exclusion list (read in full before publishing page copy — extraction pass focused on benefits).
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · pp.23–25

aia.value: No ceasing age identified on first pass — VERIFY in §G/defined terms.
aia.source: AIA Private Health umbrella wording v6 (eff. 17 Apr 2025) · needs second pass

pl.value: Surgical Benefit: up to $300,000 per life assured per policy year (surgeon/anaesthetist/theatre/hospital fees, prostheses, related consults/diagnostics/prescriptions/physio within 6 months). Includes oral surgery, medically-required weight-loss surgery, breast reconstruction after cancer with no time limit.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.1, p.2–3

pl.value: Non-surgical Benefit: up to $300,000 per life assured per policy year, covering Private Hospital admissions (§4.2.1) and the Serious Illness Benefit (§4.2.2 — drug/radiotherapy treatment for life-threatening conditions e.g. cancer).
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.2, p.3–4

pl.value: Excess per Policy Schedule (options chosen at application — VERIFY current options externally). Distinctive: Excess Waiver Benefit — excess waived entirely for heart attack, stroke, coronary artery surgery, or critical cancer admissions (§5.12). Major Diagnostic excess capped at $250. Multiple Policy Excess Benefit reduces excess if another insurer paid part.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §3.3, 4.3, 5.12

pl.value: Cancer: surgery under Surgical Benefit ($300k); non-surgical cancer treatment under Serious Illness Benefit within the $300k Non-surgical maximum (chemo/radiotherapy incl. private outpatient clinic administration, prescriptions, follow-ups until cured/in remission).
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.2.2, p.3–4

pl.value: Non-Pharmac Subsidised Drugs Benefit: ALL Medsafe-registered drugs covered when prescribed by a specialist for a covered treatment, within Medsafe guidelines — paid within the Surgical/Non-surgical maximums (up to $300k), not a separate low cap. One of the strongest non-Pharmac positions in the market at this product tier.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.5, p.6

pl.value: Serious Illness follow-ups covered until cured or in remission (no fixed time window); surgery follow-ups within 6 months; Second Opinion Benefit $4,000/yr, no excess.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.1, 4.2.2, 5.11

pl.value: No standalone specialist consult benefit in base cover (consults covered when tied to surgery/admission within 6 months). Optional Specialist and Tests Benefit: $4,000/yr specialists + $4,000/yr tests (own $250 excess); 'specialist' here includes osteopath, naturopath, homeopath, chiropractor, acupuncturist.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.1, 7.1

pl.value: Major Diagnostic Benefit: $200,000 per life per policy year for specialist-recommended diagnostics (MRI, CT, PET, colonoscopy, angiogram etc.) not tied to a surgery/admission; diagnosis-purpose only (screening/surveillance excluded); excess capped at $250.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.3, p.4

pl.value: 6-month windows: pre-surgery diagnostics, pre/post consults, post prescriptions/tests/physio all within 6 months of the surgery or admission. Diagnostics leading to treatment within 6 months are re-counted under the Surgical/Non-surgical maximums.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.1–4.3

pl.value: Underwritten at application (exclusions/loadings per Policy Schedule). Children: automatically covered free for first 3 months from birth; can continue without health assessment if registered in time — effectively covering newborns before underwriting, a notable family feature.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §2, 5.1

pl.value: Sterilisation loyalty benefit after 2 years of premiums (prior approval required). Suicide-related Funeral Support exclusion first 13 months. No other general stand-downs identified.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §6.1, 9

pl.value: All known congenital conditions excluded (inherited or external-factor), with no exception list — stricter than SC/nib/AIA on congenital.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §9, p.12

pl.value: No GP/day-to-day module. GP, dentist, nurse, physio and prescription costs explicitly excluded except where tied to covered treatment. Optional Specialist & Tests Benefit is the only day-to-day-adjacent add-on.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §7.1, 9

pl.value: Normal pregnancy, childbirth, caesareans, infertility all excluded. Obstetrician costs covered ONLY under the optional Specialist & Tests Benefit for complications of pregnancy (until 90 days post-pregnancy).
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §7.1, 9

pl.value: Psychiatric conditions and mental health disorders explicitly excluded — the clearest mental-health exclusion among the five insurers.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §9, p.12

pl.value: Not in wording — no telehealth provision identified.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · not found

pl.value: Prostheses covered within Surgical Benefit when required as a result of surgery (within the $300k maximum; no separate schedule cited).
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §4.1

pl.value: 'Approved' private hospitals/facilities; usual-customary-reasonable pricing test applies. Unique: Australasian coverage — treatment in Australia reimbursed at NZ-equivalent rates; Medical Tourism Benefit reimburses 75% of NZ cost if you choose treatment overseas; Overseas Waiting List Benefit if NZ private care unavailable within 6 months.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §3.4, 4.4

pl.value: Pre-approval preferred but not mandatory (reimbursement claims accepted at claimant's risk). Prior approval required for sterilisation loyalty benefit.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §8, 6.1

pl.value: Paper-leaning process: claim form + original invoices to Partners Life (fax/email to start, originals required to pay). Contact 0800 145 433 or via adviser.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §8, 10

pl.value: Loyalty: sterilisation after 2 years. Extras others don't have: Waiver of Premium on death of a life assured (3 yrs premiums refunded for survivors), Funeral Support $3,500, Medical Misadventure $30,000, Public Hospital Cash Grant $300/night (nights 4–13), Hospice Benefit $300/night.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §5.2, 5.7–5.10, 6.1

pl.value: Not stated in wording. Partners Life announced Journey Plan PMC premium +2.0% and policy fee $66.05/yr from 22 Apr 2026 — cite externally. EXTERNAL VERIFICATION NEEDED.
pl.source: External — riskinfonz.co.nz Mar 2026 + PL rate card

pl.value: Children converting to their own policy get existing-or-current terms, whichever is MORE FAVOURABLE — a pro-customer conversion promise. General upgrade pass-back not stated — VERIFY.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §5.1

pl.value: Extensive exclusion list: mental health, congenital (all), GP/dental/prescriptions (unless specified), normal pregnancy/caesareans, preventative care/screening, sleep apnoea investigations, laser eye, alcohol/drug-related, geriatric care, emergency acute care (public system's role), war/terrorism, criminal-offence injuries.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §9, p.12–13

pl.value: No ceasing age for adults identified; children may remain covered at any age while premiums paid. VERIFY whether current sold product (Journey Plan) differs — THIS DOC IS V11 of the prior-generation product; confirm current version with Partners Life/adviser before publishing.
pl.source: Partners Life Private Medical Cover Protection Benefit Sheet V11 · §5.1 + version note

uni.value: Surgery: 'No Maximum' per admission — 100% of reasonable charges for non-acute qualifying surgical procedures in licensed private hospitals (surgeon, anaesthetist, hospital, prostheses, ICU). Sub-limits: spinal surgery $200,000 lifetime; oral surgery no maximum; breast reconstruction no maximum. Excess applies.
uni.source: Hospital Select Plus Modules Plan (COREBUS 01.08.25, eff. 1 Aug 2025) · Surgery section, pp.2–3

uni.value: Medical Hospitalisation: $65,000 per policy year (non-acute, excludes psychiatric/geriatric) + $500 ancillary. Acute private hospitalisation grant $5,000/yr. Psychiatric/geriatric hospitalisation $5,000/yr.
uni.source: Hospital Select Plus Modules Plan (COREBUS 01.08.25, eff. 1 Aug 2025) · Private Hospitalisation, p.4

uni.value: Voluntary excess option applies PER CLAIM (not per year — differs from SC/nib/AIA annual excesses). Amount per Membership Certificate; benefits show where excess applies. Worth a 'what this means' explainer — per-claim excess changes the maths for multiple claims in a year.
uni.source: UniMed T&C 2026 · 'How an excess works', p.13

uni.value: Chemotherapy: $65,000/yr (Pharmac drugs, oncologist treatment, hospital costs; includes genetic/genomic testing post-diagnosis). Radiation oncology: $65,000/yr. Cancer surgery under the no-maximum Surgery benefit.
uni.source: Hospital Select Plus Modules Plan (COREBUS 01.08.25, eff. 1 Aug 2025) · Private Hospitalisation, p.4

uni.value: Non-Pharmac: chemo drugs (Medsafe-approved) up to $10,000/yr within the Chemotherapy benefit; PLUS separate In-Patient Non-Pharmac Subsidised Pharmaceuticals $2,000/yr (any condition, not just cancer); Day-to-Day module adds $1,000/yr non-Pharmac scripts.
uni.source: Hospital Select Plus Modules Plan (COREBUS 01.08.25, eff. 1 Aug 2025) · pp.2, 4 + Module G

uni.value: Surveillance Following Cancer Treatment: specialist consults + investigations for 5 YEARS post-treatment, $3,000/yr — the longest defined cancer-surveillance window among the five.
uni.source: Hospital Select Plus Modules Plan (COREBUS 01.08.25, eff. 1 Aug 2025) · p.4
